recreation_prompt_markdown:
# Recreation Prompt

Create a single-file browser game called **Caller ID: Final Cut**. It should preserve the mechanics of a mobile auto-battle roster simulator: two teams, per-unit roster counts capped at 15, an HP/tension slider, a start button, autonomous canvas combat, team health bars, pause/audio/menu controls, result overlay, restart, summons, projectiles, blocks, and special domain-like events.

Reinterpret those mechanics as a Scream-inspired meta-horror mystery. The player builds a Final Cut survivor roster and a Copycat Alibi roster on a suspect board, then taps **Answer the Call**. Units are teen slasher archetypes: Final Girl, Ghostface Prime, Phone Nerd, Red Herring, Rule Breaker, Legacy Survivor, and similar roles. The battle happens on a portrait-first suburban night playfield with procedural houses, phone wires, moving police tape, VHS scanlines, mask/knife silhouettes, call-trace glows, and self-aware slasher trope popups.

Use browser-native Canvas, CSS, DOM, and vanilla JS. Keep mobile readability and touch targets clear. The finished surface must feel like a public-facing meta-horror game, not a generic arena with horror labels.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: mobile-first canvas auto-battle roster simulator.
- objective: configure two opposing rosters within a 15-unit cap, choose an HP/tension scale, start the match, and watch autonomous units fight until one side has no non-summoned survivors.
- input model: tap/click plus/minus roster cards, HP range slider, start, pause, audio toggle, menu, restart; no direct movement control during battle.
- core loop: select units -> start canvas battle -> entities spawn left/right -> AI moves toward nearest enemy -> attacks/skills/projectiles/domain events resolve damage -> team HP HUD updates -> result overlay offers redial/restart or return.
- fail/friction state: a team loses when its original units are dead; draw is possible if both sides fall; roster start button disables if either side has zero units; pause can interrupt active simulation.

## Protected mechanics
- Team limit of 15 per side and per-unit count modification semantics.
- HP multiplier slider values, including very high/endless/glass modes.
- Autonomous battle loop timing via requestAnimationFrame, entity movement, gravity/floor, targeting, cooldowns, projectiles, block chance, stun, summons, domain events, shake/freeze feedback, and win-condition checks.
- HUD team health bars and result/restart/menu state transitions.
- Mobile tap/click paths for setup, info, start, pause, audio, menu, and restart.

## Remixed target
Caller ID: Final Cut reframes the auto-battle as a self-aware teen slasher mystery. The player builds a survivor-side suspect board against a copycat Ghostface-side alibi board, answers the phone, and watches slasher tropes collide. The focal identity is a phone-call/cassette/masked-caller system: survivors, red herrings, and copycats battle on a procedural suburban horror set with phone wires, crime-scene tape, jump-cut popups, and meta genre jokes. Mechanics remain the same; presentation, copy, procedural drawing, HUD vocabulary, and atmosphere are transformed for portrait mobile play.
